newsitem.title: UK: Major in thrall to party's Eurosceptics - UK's Cook.
newsitem.headline: Major in thrall to party's Eurosceptics - UK's Cook.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party on Wednesday accused Prime Minister John Major of having given way to demands from his party's Eurosceptics despite the risk to Britain's economy from bad relations with its European partners.
"The Eurosceptics have won the war in the Tory Party," Foreign Affairs spokesman Robin Cook said in a keynote speech in London on the European Union.
He said shortly after the 1992 general election Major had said it would be wrong for Britain to "stand on the outskirts of Europe as an island, tossing bricks at it".

"John Major finishes the same parliamentary term trying to prove he can toss bricks at Europe as fast as Teresa Gorman or Teddy Taylor," he said, referring to two prominent Conservative Eurosceptic members of parliament.
"The crisis in our relations with the rest of Europe reflects a crisis of leadership in the British government," Cook added.
"The tragedy for Britain is that it is our jobs, exports and incomes that would be at risk in the crisis which the Tory Eurosceptics crave with Europe."
Cook compared the Eurosceptics to the Militant Tendency whose Trotskyite members infiltrated Labour in the 1980s, pushing it towards socialist policies which made it unelectable.
"The difference between the Labour Party and the Conservative Party is that Labour's leadership took on the Militant Tendency and crushed them," he said.
"The Tory leadership has surrendered to the Eurosceptics without even a fight." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7767
